entries.title: Stealth
entries.body:
# Stealth

## Overview

Stealth Skill Techniques represent specialised methods of remaining unseen, moving silently, concealing evidence and avoiding detection through mastery of the **Stealth** skill.

Stealth is more than simply hiding behind an object. A skilled practitioner learns how light, sound, movement and attention shape what others perceive. They understand when to move, where to place their weight and how to use terrain, crowds and distractions to disappear from notice.

Novices learn to control their footsteps and remain still within basic concealment. As their mastery grows, they learn to cross exposed spaces, vanish within crowds, conceal their trail and move through guarded areas without alerting nearby creatures.

Legendary practitioners can pass through places others consider impossible to infiltrate, becoming little more than a fleeting shadow or a forgotten movement at the edge of sight.

Whenever a character reaches a new **Stealth Skill Rank**, they may choose **one technique** from the four techniques available at that rank.

Once selected, a technique becomes part of the character's Stealth training unless it is replaced through retraining approved by the GM.

Stealth Techniques are **Skill Techniques**, not Talents. They do not normally have an inherent resource cost. Prolonged concealment, difficult movement, extreme physical control or repeated attempts under pressure may still cause Stamina loss or Exhaustion.

---

**Primary Characteristic:** Agility  
**Secondary Characteristic:** Dexterity

## Ranks

### Learning Techniques

| Skill Rank | Techniques Available | Techniques Learned |
|---|---:|---:|
| Novice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Initiate | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Apprentice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Journeyman | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Adept | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Master | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Grandmaster | 4 | Choose 1 |

**Maximum Techniques Known:** **7**

---

### Novice Techniques

> The Novice learns that stillness is as important as movement.  
> A hidden figure is often revealed not by being seen, but by moving at the wrong moment.

#### Soft Step

You carefully control where and how your feet touch the ground.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when moving quietly across ordinary terrain.
- Reduce noise caused by loose stones, floorboards and light debris.
- Recognise surfaces that are likely to create excessive sound.
- Running or moving through heavily obstructed terrain may remove this benefit.

---

#### Stillness

You remain motionless while observation passes over your hiding place.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when remaining hidden without moving.
- Minor discomfort does not immediately force you to shift position.
- Reduce the chance of being noticed through small involuntary movements.
- The benefit ends when you attack, speak loudly or leave concealment.

---

#### Basic Concealment

You understand how to use shadows, furniture and natural cover to hide your body.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when hiding behind suitable physical concealment.
- Quickly identify nearby locations capable of hiding a creature of your size.
- Reduce penalties caused by imperfect but usable cover.
- This technique cannot conceal you in a completely open and brightly lit area.

---

#### Quiet Hands

You have learned to handle common objects without unnecessary sound.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when opening ordinary doors, containers and windows quietly.
- Reduce noise caused by drawing weapons or retrieving small items.
- Recognise loose fittings, hinges and objects likely to rattle.
- Damaged or trapped mechanisms may still produce unavoidable noise.

---

### Initiate Techniques

> The Initiate learns to move with the rhythm of the world around them.  
> A closing door, passing cart or gust of wind becomes an opportunity to disappear.

#### Shadow Movement

You use dim light and shifting shadows to conceal your movement.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when moving through dimly lit areas.
- Reduce the chance of being noticed when moving between nearby shadows.
- Recognise when changing light will briefly expose your position.
- Bright magical illumination may prevent this technique from functioning.

---

#### Sound Masking

You time your movement to coincide with surrounding noise.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when moving during rain, conversation, machinery or other significant sounds.
- Reduce penalties caused by crossing a noisy surface.
- Recognise repeating sounds that can be used to conceal your movement.
- Sudden silence may reveal you if you continue moving carelessly.

---

#### Low Profile

You reduce the amount of your body exposed while moving.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when remaining hidden behind low cover.
- Move through crouched or confined positions with reduced penalties.
- Reduce the chance of being seen over barriers and furniture.
- Your Movement may be reduced while maintaining the posture.

---

#### Concealed Equipment

You secure your belongings so they do not betray your presence.

**Effects**
- Reduce noise from armour, weapons, containers and carried equipment.
- Gain Advantage when preparing equipment for infiltration.
- Recognise items likely to reflect light or create sound.
- Heavy or poorly fitted equipment may still impose Stealth penalties.

---

### Apprentice Techniques

> The Apprentice understands that attention is limited.  
> The easiest path is not always unseen—it is simply the path no one thinks to watch.

#### Distracted Passage

You move while nearby creatures are focused elsewhere.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when hiding or moving while observers are distracted.
- Reduce penalties when crossing a briefly exposed space during a distraction.
- Recognise when a creature's attention has shifted away from your position.
- The benefit ends if you become the direct focus of observation.

---

#### Crowd Blend

You conceal yourself by adopting the pace and behaviour of those around you.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when hiding within a crowd or busy settlement.
- Reduce the chance of being remembered by casual witnesses.
- Match the movement and apparent purpose of nearby people.
- Distinctive clothing, behaviour or physical features may reduce the benefit.

---

#### Hidden Approach

You carefully close the distance to an unaware creature.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when approaching a creature that has not detected you.
- Reduce the penalty for moving through the edge of its hearing range.
- Recognise the direction in which the creature's attention is focused.
- The benefit ends if you Sprint or cross terrain without concealment.

---

#### Leave No Trace

You minimise signs left behind by your movement.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when concealing footprints, disturbed objects and minor environmental signs.
- Reduce the chance of ordinary trackers identifying your route.
- Recognise when your clothing or equipment has left visible evidence.
- This technique does not erase blood, strong scent or magical residue.

---

### Journeyman Techniques

> The Journeyman no longer relies upon a single hiding place.  
> Every room, alley and forest path becomes a collection of unseen routes.

#### Silent Takedown

You subdue an unaware target before they can raise an alarm.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when attempting to Grapple or incapacitate an unaware adjacent creature.
- On success, the target cannot immediately call out.
- The technique may be used with a suitable non-lethal attack.
- Powerful, alert or physically superior creatures may resist normally.

---

#### Guard Pattern

You study the habits and blind spots of patrolling creatures.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when moving through an area after observing its guards.
- Identify repeating patrol routes, pauses and changes of direction.
- Recognise positions that guards consistently fail to watch.
- Unpredictable or magically coordinated guards may be harder to analyse.

---

#### Silent Climb

You can climb without creating obvious sound or debris.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage on Stealth checks made while climbing.
- Reduce noise caused by ropes, handholds and loose surfaces.
- Recognise unstable sections before placing your weight upon them.
- This technique does not replace an appropriate Climbing check.

---

#### Vanishing Turn

You break line of sight and immediately change direction.

**Effects**
- After leaving an observer's line of sight, gain Advantage on your next Stealth check.
- Creatures searching for you are more likely to continue toward your previous route.
- You may move up to **5 ft** in a different direction after entering concealment.
- The benefit is lost if the observer can clearly track your movement.

---

### Adept Techniques

> The Adept understands perception as a weapon.  
> They hide not only their body, but the very expectation that someone is present.

#### Unseen Movement

You maintain concealment while moving at greater speed.

**Effects**
- Move up to your normal Movement without automatically losing Stealth.
- Reduce penalties caused by moving quickly between concealed positions.
- Gain Advantage when crossing a short gap between areas of cover.
- Sprinting remains difficult to conceal without a suitable distraction.

---

#### Blind-Side Passage

You remain within the areas an observer is least capable of watching.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when moving outside a creature's direct field of vision.
- Recognise when an observer's equipment, anatomy or posture creates a blind side.
- Reduce penalties when passing close to a distracted creature.
- Creatures with supernatural awareness may not possess an exploitable blind side.

---

#### Hidden in Plain Sight

You use posture, timing and environmental familiarity to avoid attention without full cover.

**Effects**
- Attempt to remain unnoticed in an area where you have plausible reason to be present.
- Gain Advantage when disguising your purpose through ordinary behaviour.
- Casual observers are less likely to question or remember you.
- Direct inspection or behaviour that contradicts your surroundings may reveal you.

---

#### Predator's Silence

You conceal the final stages of your approach toward prey.

**Effects**
- Creatures you approach from concealment suffer Disadvantage when attempting to hear you.
- Gain Advantage on Stealth checks made within short range of an unaware target.
- Reduce noise caused by drawing a weapon immediately before attacking.
- The technique ends after you attack or are detected.

---

### Master Techniques

> The Master moves through guarded places as though they were built with hidden paths only they can see.  
> Locks, lanterns and watchful eyes become parts of a pattern rather than obstacles.

#### Ghost Walk

You move through difficult environments with almost no disturbance.

**Effects**
- Ignore ordinary Stealth penalties caused by vegetation, shallow water and loose ground.
- Reduce signs left by your passage.
- Gain Advantage when moving through terrain that would normally reveal a creature.
- Extreme conditions and magical terrain may still impose penalties.

---

#### Perfect Timing

You recognise the exact moment when every observer is least prepared to notice you.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, gain Advantage on a Stealth check without requiring concealment from every observer.
- Move through a briefly exposed area before nearby creatures can react.
- Observers must be distracted, repositioning or otherwise experiencing a momentary lapse.
- This technique does not function against creatures directly watching you without interruption.

---

#### Misdirected Search

You manipulate evidence so pursuers search in the wrong direction.

**Effects**
- Create a believable false route using disturbed terrain, moved objects or planted evidence.
- Gain Advantage when directing searchers away from your true path.
- Creatures that fail to recognise the deception lose additional time following the false trail.
- Skilled trackers may contest the deception using Tracking.

---

#### Silent Assault

You preserve your concealment during the opening moments of combat.

**Effects**
- After attacking from Stealth, immediately attempt a new Stealth check if suitable concealment is available.
- Reduce the chance that distant enemies identify your exact position.
- You may shift **5 ft** after the attack without provoking an ordinary Reaction.
- Loud weapons, obvious magic or open terrain may prevent concealment.

---

### Grandmaster Techniques

> The Grandmaster leaves no image in the eye, no sound in the ear and no certainty in the mind.  
> Those who sense their presence do so only after the moment has already passed.

#### Presence Without Trace

Your movement leaves almost no ordinary evidence.

**Effects**
- Ordinary observers cannot reliably identify your footprints, scent or route.
- Gain Advantage against Tracking checks made to follow you.
- Minor signs of your passage naturally blend into the environment.
- Blood, powerful magic and deliberate destruction may still reveal your presence.

---

#### Between Heartbeats

You cross an exposed space during a moment too brief for ordinary awareness.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, move up to half your Movement between two areas of concealment.
- Ordinary observers cannot make Reactions against this movement.
- You remain hidden if no observer possesses an uninterrupted view of the entire route.
- Supernatural perception may still detect your passage.

---

#### Forgotten Face

Your presence becomes extraordinarily difficult for witnesses to remember accurately.

**Effects**
- Casual witnesses struggle to recall your clothing, features and direction of travel.
- Gain Advantage when avoiding later identification.
- Descriptions of you given by ordinary observers are incomplete or contradictory.
- This technique does not alter memories magically or affect someone who studied you closely.

---

#### Living Shadow

You have achieved legendary mastery of concealment and silent movement.

**Effects**
- The first Stealth check you make each encounter has Advantage.
- Ordinary movement does not automatically break Stealth while suitable concealment exists.
- Once per encounter, reroll a failed Stealth check and use the new result.
- Creatures relying only upon ordinary sight and hearing suffer Disadvantage when attempting to locate you.
- Magical detection and specialised senses may still reveal your position.

---

> *"True stealth is not the absence of sound. It is the absence of suspicion."*

## Checks

Use **Agility** as the primary characteristic and **Dexterity** as the supporting characteristic when the GM calls for a Stealth check.

entries.title: Archery
entries.body:
# Archery

## Overview

Archery Skill Techniques represent specialised methods of aiming, firing, repositioning and controlling the battlefield through mastery of the **Archery** skill.

An archer learns far more than how to release an arrow. Skilled archers judge distance, account for movement, fire from difficult positions and exploit brief openings in an enemy's defence. As their mastery grows, they may pierce armour, strike distant targets, fire several arrows in rapid succession and perform legendary shots that appear almost impossible.

Whenever a character reaches a new **Archery Skill Rank**, they may choose **one technique** from the four techniques available at that rank.

Once selected, a technique becomes part of the character's archery training unless it is replaced through retraining approved by the GM.

Archery Techniques are **Skill Techniques**, not Talents. They do not normally have an inherent resource cost. Particularly demanding techniques may require additional Action Points, specialised ammunition or Stamina when the character is firing repeatedly or pushing beyond normal physical limits.

---

**Primary Characteristic:** Dexterity  
**Secondary Characteristic:** Agility

## Ranks

### Learning Techniques

| Skill Rank | Techniques Available | Techniques Learned |
|---|---:|---:|
| Novice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Initiate | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Apprentice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Journeyman | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Adept | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Master | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Grandmaster | 4 | Choose 1 |

**Maximum Techniques Known:** **7**

---

### Novice Techniques

#### Steady Draw

You control your breathing and maintain a stable draw.

**Effects**
- Gain **+1 Accuracy** with Archery attacks when you have not moved during the current turn.
- Minor environmental distractions do not interrupt your aim.
- The bonus ends after the attack is made.

---

#### Quick Nock

You can prepare an arrow with practiced speed.

**Effects**
- Reduce the time required to draw and nock an arrow.
- Gain Advantage on checks made to ready a bow under pressure.
- You may draw ammunition without interrupting ordinary movement.

---

#### Hunter's Eye

You have learned to recognise exposed areas on a target.

**Effects**
- Gain **+1 Damage** against creatures that are unaware of you.
- Gain Advantage when identifying an obvious unarmoured area on a visible target.
- This technique does not reveal hidden anatomical weaknesses.

---

#### Anchored Stance

You position your body to absorb the bow's strain.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage against effects that would disrupt your Archery attack.
- Reduce penalties caused by minor shaking, unstable footing or strong recoil.
- You lose this benefit if you are knocked Prone.

---

### Initiate Techniques

#### Longshot

You have learned to maintain accuracy over greater distances.

**Effects**
- Increase the effective range of bows you wield.
- Reduce the first range penalty applied to your Archery attacks.
- Gain Advantage when estimating the distance to a visible target.

---

#### Moving Shot

You can fire while repositioning.

**Effects**
- Moving up to half your normal Movement does not impose a penalty on Archery attacks.
- Gain Advantage when maintaining aim while walking or changing position.
- Sprinting or forced movement may still disrupt your shot.

---

#### Pinning Arrow

You aim for clothing, equipment or nearby terrain to restrict movement.

**Effects**
- On a successful attack, you may attempt to pin the target to a nearby surface.
- A pinned target must use an action or succeed on a Strength check to free itself.
- Creatures without clothing, armour or an appropriate nearby surface cannot be pinned.
- The technique may deal reduced damage at the GM's discretion.

---

#### Controlled Release

You release the bowstring at the exact moment your aim settles.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, ignore **1 point of Accuracy penalty** affecting an Archery attack.
- Reduce penalties caused by minor cover or poor visibility.
- This technique cannot overcome complete concealment.

---

### Apprentice Techniques

#### Piercing Shot

You align your arrow to penetrate protective materials.

**Effects**
- Ignore **2 Armour** with Archery attacks.
- Deal increased damage against lightly armoured targets.
- This technique does not ignore Natural Armour unless specifically allowed by the GM.

---

#### Rapid Shot

You can release a second arrow before your opponent reacts.

**Effects**
- Once per round, spend an additional **Action Point** to make a second Archery attack.
- The second attack suffers **-2 Accuracy**.
- Both attacks must target creatures within your bow's effective range.

---

#### Hamstring Shot

You target the legs to hinder an enemy's movement.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, a creature damaged by your arrow loses **10 ft Movement** until the end of its next turn.
- A Critical Hit may extend the movement penalty for an additional turn.
- Creatures without vulnerable limbs may be immune.

---

#### Covering Fire

You fire into an area to limit enemy movement.

**Effects**
- Choose a visible area within your bow's effective range.
- Enemies moving through the area risk an immediate Archery attack.
- The effect lasts until the start of your next turn.
- You must have available ammunition and a clear line of sight.

---

### Journeyman Techniques

#### Ricochet Shot

You can redirect an arrow from a solid surface.

**Effects**
- Make an Archery attack against a target behind partial cover by ricocheting the arrow.
- The attack suffers **-2 Accuracy**.
- The arrow requires an appropriate hard surface and a believable angle.
- This technique cannot strike targets behind complete sealed cover.

---

#### Eagle's Focus

You remain fixed upon a distant target.

**Effects**
- Spend one Action Point to focus on a visible creature.
- Gain **+2 Accuracy** against that creature until you change targets, lose sight of it or move more than half your Movement.
- The bonus does not stack with itself.

---

#### Disarming Shot

You aim for an opponent's weapon or held object.

**Effects**
- Make an Archery attack against an object held by a visible creature.
- On success, the creature must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity check or drop the object.
- The attack may damage fragile objects.
- Large or securely held objects are more difficult to disarm.

---

#### Split Arrow

You strike an incoming projectile or vulnerable object with your own arrow.

**Effects**
- Use your Reaction to attempt an Archery check against a visible non-magical projectile.
- On success, the projectile is deflected or destroyed.
- You must be aware of the projectile and have a prepared bow.
- Siege ammunition and massive projectiles cannot normally be stopped.

---

### Adept Techniques

#### Armour-Piercing Shot

You fire with enough precision and force to penetrate heavy protection.

**Effects**
- Ignore **4 Armour** with Archery attacks.
- Ignore **1 Natural Armour**.
- Deal increased durability damage to shields and armour struck directly.
- This technique does not stack with Piercing Shot.

---

#### Rain of Arrows

You release several arrows into a concentrated area.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** and additional ammunition to target a small area.
- Creatures within the area must defend against the attack.
- Each affected target takes reduced weapon damage.
- Cover may reduce or prevent the damage.

---

#### Deadeye

You wait for the perfect moment to release a devastating shot.

**Effects**
- Spend one Action Point aiming before making the attack.
- Gain Advantage on the attack roll.
- On a successful hit, roll one additional weapon damage die.
- Moving or taking damage before firing may interrupt the aim.

---

#### Intercepting Shot

You can disrupt an enemy as they act.

**Effects**
- Use your Reaction to make an Archery attack against a creature beginning a visible action.
- On a Critical Hit, the target must succeed on an appropriate check or have its action interrupted.
- The technique cannot interrupt instantaneous or unseen actions.
- The GM determines whether the action can reasonably be disrupted.

---

### Master Techniques

#### Penetrating Line

Your arrow passes through one enemy and continues into another.

**Effects**
- Choose two creatures standing in a straight line.
- Make one Archery attack against the first creature.
- On a successful hit, make a second attack against the creature behind it.
- The second attack deals **50% weapon damage**.

---

#### Phantom Volley

Your draw and release become difficult for enemies to follow.

**Effects**
- Make up to three Archery attacks by spending additional Action Points.
- Each attack after the first suffers a cumulative **-1 Accuracy**.
- The attacks may target the same creature or different visible creatures.
- You must have sufficient ammunition available.

---

#### Perfect Trajectory

You instinctively account for wind, distance and movement.

**Effects**
- Ignore ordinary penalties caused by wind and long range.
- Reduce penalties against moving targets.
- Gain Advantage when firing from elevated terrain.
- Severe magical weather may still affect your arrows.

---

#### Heartseeker

You target a creature's most vulnerable vital area.

**Effects**
- Spend one Action Point aiming before making the attack.
- Critical Hits deal **two additional weapon damage dice**.
- Creatures without vital organs may be immune to the additional damage.
- The technique requires an unobstructed view of the target.

---

### Grandmaster Techniques

#### Arrow of Certain Death

You release a shot intended to end the battle with one perfect strike.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to make one Archery attack with Advantage.
- Ignore all Armour granted by worn equipment.
- Roll three additional weapon damage dice on a Critical Hit.
- Bosses and legendary creatures may resist instant-kill effects.

---

#### Horizon Shot

Your arrows can strike targets at seemingly impossible distances.

**Effects**
- Greatly increase your bow's maximum range.
- Ignore normal long-range Accuracy penalties.
- You may attack a target you can clearly observe through a suitable viewing aid.
- The arrow still requires a possible physical path to the target.

---

#### Thousand Arrow Discipline

Your mastery allows you to maintain a relentless stream of arrows.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, enter the Thousand Arrow Discipline until the end of your next turn.
- Your Archery attacks require one fewer Action Point, to a minimum of one.
- You may make no more than four attacks during the technique.
- Each attack still consumes ammunition.

---

#### Unerring Archer

Your understanding of the bow has reached legendary perfection.

**Effects**
- The first Archery attack you make each round has Advantage.
- Archery attacks count as Magical for overcoming resistance.
- Ignore penalties from partial cover.
- Once per encounter, reroll a failed Archery attack and use the new result.

---

> *"The bow is silent until the moment a decision can no longer be undone."*

## Checks

Use **Dexterity** as the primary characteristic and **Agility** as the supporting characteristic when the GM calls for a Archery check.

## Training

Training techniques and rank requirements are listed in the Ranks tab.

Information coming soon.

# Crossbows

## Overview

Crossbow Skill Techniques represent specialised methods of loading, aiming, firing and maintaining crossbows through mastery of the **Crossbows** skill.

A crossbow rewards patience, mechanical understanding and precise shot placement. Unlike bows, crossbows rely less upon continuous physical draw strength and more upon preparation, stability and the proper use of their mechanisms.

Novice crossbow users learn how to load safely and fire accurately. As their mastery grows, they learn to penetrate armour, interrupt charging enemies, prepare specialised bolts and control the battlefield through carefully timed attacks.

Legendary crossbow users are capable of striking targets through narrow openings, disabling equipment and delivering devastating bolts before their enemies recognise the danger.

Whenever a character reaches a new **Crossbows Skill Rank**, they may choose **one technique** from the four techniques available at that rank.

Once selected, a technique becomes part of the character's Crossbows training unless it is replaced through retraining approved by the GM.

Crossbow Techniques are **Skill Techniques**, not Talents. They do not normally have an inherent resource cost. Techniques may still require additional Action Points, specialised bolts, suitable loading mechanisms or Stamina when the weapon is used repeatedly under pressure.

---

**Primary Characteristic:** Dexterity  
**Secondary Characteristic:** Intelligence

## Ranks

### Learning Techniques

| Skill Rank | Techniques Available | Techniques Learned |
|---|---:|---:|
| Novice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Initiate | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Apprentice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Journeyman | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Adept | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Master | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Grandmaster | 4 | Choose 1 |

**Maximum Techniques Known:** **7**

---

### Novice Techniques

> The Novice learns that a crossbow is not simply aimed and fired.  
> Every latch, string and bolt must work together before the shot can be trusted.

#### Steady Stock

You brace the weapon firmly against your body before firing.

**Effects**
- Gain **+1 Accuracy** when firing without moving during the current turn.
- Reduce penalties caused by minor shaking or unstable footing.
- The bonus ends after the attack is made.
- This technique does not function while Prone unless the weapon can be properly supported.

---

#### Safe Loading

You have learned how to load a crossbow without placing your hands or equipment at unnecessary risk.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when loading a crossbow under pressure.
- Reduce the chance of injuring yourself during an ordinary loading failure.
- Recognise when the string, latch or bolt has been positioned incorrectly.
- This technique does not protect against a broken or sabotaged mechanism.

---

#### Bolt Recognition

You understand the basic differences between common crossbow bolts.

**Effects**
- Identify common bolt types and their intended purpose.
- Recognise whether a bolt is damaged, poorly balanced or unsuitable for your crossbow.
- Gain Advantage when selecting suitable ammunition for hunting, combat or practice.
- Magical and specialised bolts may require further knowledge.

---

#### Supported Aim

You use walls, tables, shields or terrain to steady your weapon.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when firing from a properly supported position.
- Reduce one ordinary Accuracy penalty caused by distance or instability.
- The support must be strong enough to hold the weapon steady.
- Moving away from the support ends the benefit.

---

### Initiate Techniques

> The Initiate begins to understand the weapon’s rhythm.  
> Loading, aiming and firing become one continuous mechanical discipline.

#### Practised Reload

You can reset and reload your crossbow with greater efficiency.

**Effects**
- Reduce the Action Point cost or time required to reload by one step, to the minimum allowed by the weapon.
- Gain Advantage when reloading while moving no more than half your Movement.
- You may retrieve a bolt without interrupting the reload.
- Heavy siege crossbows may not benefit fully from this technique.

---

#### Long Bolt

You adjust your firing angle for distant targets.

**Effects**
- Increase the effective range of crossbows you wield.
- Reduce the first long-range Accuracy penalty.
- Gain Advantage when estimating the distance to a stationary target.
- Severe wind or poor visibility may still impose penalties.

---

#### Braced Shot

You lock your stance before releasing a powerful shot.

**Effects**
- Spend an additional **Action Point** before making the attack.
- Gain **+2 Damage** on a successful hit.
- Ignore **1 Armour**.
- You cannot move after preparing the shot until the attack is completed.

---

#### Mechanism Familiarity

You understand how ordinary crossbow components fit and operate.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when inspecting a crossbow for mechanical faults.
- Perform basic repairs on strings, triggers, latches and loading mechanisms.
- Reduce the time required to clear an ordinary jam.
- Complex magical or repeating crossbows may require Engineering or another appropriate skill.

---

### Apprentice Techniques

> The Apprentice no longer waits for an obvious target.  
> They create openings by controlling when and where the bolt is released.

#### Armour-Piercing Bolt

You align a heavy bolt with gaps and weak points in armour.

**Effects**
- Ignore **2 Armour** with Crossbow attacks.
- Gain **+1 Damage** against targets wearing Medium or Heavy Armour.
- This technique requires a suitable solid bolt.
- It does not ignore Natural Armour unless another effect allows it.

---

#### Pinning Shot

You fire through clothing, equipment or limbs to restrict movement.

**Effects**
- On a successful attack, you may attempt to pin the target to a nearby surface.
- The target must use an action or succeed on a Strength check to free itself.
- The attack may deal reduced damage at the GM's discretion.
- The target must be close enough to an appropriate surface.

---

#### Prepared Shot

You wait with the crossbow trained upon a specific area.

**Effects**
- Choose a visible creature, doorway or small area within range.
- Make a Crossbow attack as a Reaction when the chosen trigger occurs.
- Gain **+1 Accuracy** on the triggered attack.
- The preparation ends if you move, become unable to see the area or take another major action.

---

#### Crippling Bolt

You target the legs, wings or other movement structures.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, a creature damaged by your bolt loses **10 ft Movement** until the end of its next turn.
- A Critical Hit prevents the target from Sprinting during that time.
- Flying creatures struck in a wing may be forced to descend at the GM's discretion.
- Creatures without vulnerable movement structures may be immune.

---

### Journeyman Techniques

> The Journeyman treats every bolt as a deliberate answer.  
> They do not fire often, but each release changes the shape of the battle.

#### Interrupting Shot

You fire the moment an enemy exposes itself during an action.

**Effects**
- Use your Reaction to attack a visible creature beginning a deliberate action.
- On a Critical Hit, the target must succeed on an appropriate check or have the action interrupted.
- The technique cannot interrupt instantaneous or unseen actions.
- You must have a loaded crossbow.

---

#### Penetrating Bolt

Your bolt carries enough force to pass through one target and continue onward.

**Effects**
- Choose two creatures standing in a straight line.
- Make one Crossbow attack against the first creature.
- On a successful hit, make a second attack against the creature behind it.
- The second attack deals **50% weapon damage**.
- Particularly large or heavily armoured targets may stop the bolt.

---

#### Disabling Shot

You target weapons, equipment and mechanical components.

**Effects**
- Make a Crossbow attack against a visible held object or exposed mechanism.
- On success, the item may be dropped, damaged or temporarily disabled.
- Gain Advantage when targeting fragile ropes, locks, levers or exposed components.
- The GM determines the durability and exact result.

---

#### Concealed Shooter

You minimise the signs that reveal your firing position.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage on Stealth checks made immediately after firing from concealment.
- Reduce the chance that enemies identify your exact location from a single shot.
- You may reposition up to **5 ft** after firing while remaining concealed.
- Bright muzzle effects, magical bolts or exposed positions may remove this benefit.

---

### Adept Techniques

> The Adept understands that the crossbow’s greatest strength is certainty.  
> The weapon is prepared slowly so that the bolt may act without hesitation.

#### Heavy Penetrator

You fire reinforced bolts capable of defeating substantial protection.

**Effects**
- Ignore **4 Armour** with Crossbow attacks.
- Ignore **1 Natural Armour**.
- Deal increased durability damage to shields and armour.
- This technique does not stack with Armour-Piercing Bolt.

---

#### Repeating Discipline

You have mastered a repeating or rapid-loading crossbow mechanism.

**Effects**
- Make one additional Crossbow attack by spending an additional **Action Point**.
- The second attack suffers **-2 Accuracy**.
- Both attacks must be made using a crossbow capable of rapid or repeated firing.
- Each attack consumes ammunition.

---

#### Anchor Bolt

You fire a heavy bolt attached to a rope, chain or reinforced line.

**Effects**
- Secure a line to suitable wood, stone, structures or large creatures.
- Gain Advantage when creating climbing lines or securing objects at range.
- Against a creature, the bolt may limit movement until removed.
- The line and bolt must be prepared before firing.

---

#### Executioner's Aim

You take additional time to place a bolt through a vital opening.

**Effects**
- Spend one **Action Point** aiming before making the attack.
- Gain Advantage on the attack roll.
- On a successful hit, roll one additional weapon damage die.
- The aim is interrupted if you move, lose sight of the target or suffer significant damage.

---

### Master Techniques

> The Master can read distance, armour and movement through the frame of the crossbow.  
> By the time the target hears the string, the decision has already been made.

#### Siege Bolt

You prepare an exceptionally heavy shot against large creatures and structures.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to make one Crossbow attack.
- Deal two additional weapon damage dice.
- Ignore half of the target's Armour.
- Deal increased damage against structures, siege engines and Large or larger creatures.
- Requires suitable heavy ammunition.

---

#### Perfect Mechanism

You maintain and operate crossbows with almost no wasted motion.

**Effects**
- Ignore ordinary penalties caused by weapon wear or minor mechanical imperfections.
- Once per round, reduce the reload requirement by one additional step.
- Gain Advantage when clearing a jam or repairing a damaged loading mechanism.
- The technique cannot restore a destroyed crossbow during combat.

---

#### Bolt Through Shadow

You strike targets concealed behind narrow openings and partial protection.

**Effects**
- Ignore penalties from partial cover.
- Reduce the penalty from heavy cover when part of the target remains visible.
- Gain Advantage when firing through narrow gaps or prepared firing slits.
- Complete cover cannot be bypassed.

---

#### Relentless Marksman

You maintain pressure by firing as soon as the mechanism is ready.

**Effects**
- When you reduce a creature to zero Health with a Crossbow attack, immediately begin reloading.
- If the crossbow becomes loaded during the same turn, gain **+1 Accuracy** on your next shot.
- The bonus lasts until the end of your next turn.
- This benefit may activate once per round.

---

### Grandmaster Techniques

> The Grandmaster does not merely fire a bolt.  
> They calculate a path through distance, armour and fate, then allow the mechanism to complete the answer.

#### Bolt of Final Judgement

You release a single devastating bolt intended to end the confrontation.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to make one Crossbow attack with Advantage.
- Ignore all Armour granted by worn equipment and shields.
- On a Critical Hit, roll three additional weapon damage dice.
- Bosses and legendary creatures may resist instant-kill or permanent injury effects.

---

#### Impossible Trajectory

You calculate shots through openings that appear too narrow or distant to use.

**Effects**
- Ignore ordinary penalties from long range, wind and partial cover.
- You may ricochet a suitable bolt from one hard surface before striking the target.
- The target must remain within the weapon's maximum range.
- The shot still requires a physically possible path.

---

#### Grand Arbalist

You have achieved legendary mastery over every ordinary crossbow design.

**Effects**
- The first Crossbow attack you make each round has Advantage.
- Crossbow attacks count as Magical for overcoming resistance.
- Reloading cannot be interrupted by ordinary distractions.
- Once per encounter, reroll a failed Crossbow attack and use the new result.

---

#### Dragon-Piercing Bolt

You prepare a shot capable of breaching the hide of enormous creatures.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage against Huge or larger creatures.
- Ignore all worn Armour and **3 Natural Armour**.
- On a Critical Hit, inflict a severe wound or roll two additional weapon damage dice.
- The technique requires a heavy crossbow and specially reinforced ammunition.

---

> *"A bow asks for strength throughout the shot. A crossbow asks only that the wielder choose the correct moment."*

## Checks

Use **Dexterity** as the primary characteristic and **Intelligence** as the supporting characteristic when the GM calls for a Crossbows check.

## Training

Training techniques and rank requirements are listed in the Ranks tab.

## Lore

Information coming soon.

## GM Notes

GM-only information coming soon.

entries.body:
# Daggers

## Overview

Dagger Skill Techniques represent specialised methods of close-range striking, rapid movement, concealment and precision learned through mastery of the **Daggers** skill.

A dagger lacks the reach and raw force of larger weapons, but its speed and flexibility make it exceptionally dangerous in skilled hands. Dagger wielders fight within an opponent's guard, target exposed areas and use brief openings that heavier weapons cannot exploit.

Novices learn safe handling, rapid strikes and close defensive movements. As their skill develops, they learn to exploit armour gaps, disable limbs, counter larger weapons and move between enemies before they can react.

Legendary dagger wielders are said to strike between heartbeats, passing through a battlefield while leaving wounds that their enemies do not notice until the blade has already vanished.

Whenever a character reaches a new **Dagger Skill Rank**, they may choose **one technique** from the four techniques available at that rank.

Once selected, a technique becomes part of the character's Dagger training unless it is replaced through retraining approved by the GM.

Dagger Techniques are **Skill Techniques**, not Talents. They do not normally have an inherent resource cost. Particularly demanding techniques may require additional Action Points or Stamina when they involve repeated attacks, extreme movement or sustained precision.

---

**Primary Characteristic:** Dexterity  
**Secondary Characteristic:** Agility

## Ranks

### Learning Techniques

| Skill Rank | Techniques Available | Techniques Learned |
|---|---:|---:|
| Novice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Initiate | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Apprentice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Journeyman | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Adept | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Master | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Grandmaster | 4 | Choose 1 |

**Maximum Techniques Known:** **7**

---

### Novice Techniques

> The Novice learns that a dagger survives through speed and control.  
> A careless wielder reaches too far; a trained hand allows the enemy to enter first.

#### Quick Jab

You make a short, direct strike without unnecessary movement.

**Effects**
- Gain **+1 Accuracy** with Dagger attacks.
- Reduce penalties caused by fighting in confined spaces.
- This benefit does not apply while Restrained or unable to move your weapon arm.
- The technique may be used with either forward or reverse grip.

---

#### Close Guard

You keep the dagger positioned to redirect attacks at extremely close range.

**Effects**
- Gain **+1 AC** against melee attacks made by adjacent creatures.
- The bonus is lost if you are disarmed.
- The bonus does not apply against attacks made with weapons that cannot be reasonably redirected.
- You must be aware of the attacker.

---

#### Concealed Blade

You know how to hide and draw a small blade without obvious preparation.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when concealing a dagger upon your body.
- Draw a concealed dagger without interrupting ordinary movement.
- Gain Advantage when attempting to keep the weapon unnoticed during a casual search.
- A thorough physical search may still discover the weapon.

---

#### Light Footwork

You remain mobile while fighting within an enemy's reach.

**Effects**
- After making a Dagger attack, shift **5 ft** without provoking an ordinary Reaction from the target.
- The movement must end in an unoccupied space.
- You cannot use this movement while Prone or Restrained.
- This technique may be used once per turn.

---

### Initiate Techniques

> The Initiate begins to understand the safety found within an opponent's reach.  
> Where longer weapons become awkward, the dagger moves freely.

#### Armour Gap

You place the blade between plates, scales and protective fittings.

**Effects**
- Ignore **1 Armour** with Dagger attacks.
- Gain **+1 Damage** against creatures wearing Medium or Heavy Armour.
- This technique does not ignore Natural Armour.
- The target must have a physically reachable armour gap.

---

#### Returning Cut

Your blade strikes again as you withdraw it.

**Effects**
- After a successful Dagger attack, deal **+1 Damage** as the blade is pulled free.
- The additional damage is part of the same attack.
- The bonus does not apply to creatures immune to piercing or slashing injuries.
- This technique may activate once per turn.

---

#### Under the Guard

You step inside the effective reach of a larger weapon.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage on your first Dagger attack against a creature wielding a two-handed or reach weapon.
- The target suffers **-1 Accuracy** when attacking you with that weapon while you remain adjacent.
- The effect ends if you leave the creature's reach.
- The creature may change weapons or reposition to remove the penalty.

---

#### Defensive Nick

A small cut disrupts an opponent before their attack fully develops.

**Effects**
- Use your Reaction when an adjacent creature begins a visible melee attack.
- Make a Dagger attack with **-2 Accuracy**.
- On a successful hit, the creature suffers **-2 Accuracy** on the triggering attack.
- The technique does not interrupt the attack completely.

---

### Apprentice Techniques

> The Apprentice does not strike where an enemy is strongest.  
> They search for the hand, the knee, the exposed seam and the instant of hesitation.

#### Bleeding Cut

You open a wound intended to continue weakening the target.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, a successful Dagger attack may inflict **Bleeding**.
- The target may resist or remove the condition according to the normal Bleeding rules.
- Critical Hits increase the severity of the Bleeding by one rank, to the allowed maximum.
- Creatures without blood or vulnerable tissue may be immune.

---

#### Tendon Strike

You target the structures responsible for movement.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, a creature damaged by your dagger loses **10 ft Movement** until the end of its next turn.
- On a Critical Hit, the target cannot Sprint during that time.
- The target must possess vulnerable limbs or equivalent movement structures.
- This technique cannot reduce Movement below the system's minimum.

---

#### Off-Hand Discipline

You train to fight with a dagger alongside another one-handed weapon.

**Effects**
- Reduce the ordinary penalty for using a dagger in your off hand.
- Draw both weapons as part of the same preparation.
- Gain Advantage when resisting attempts to disarm your off-hand dagger.
- This technique does not grant an additional attack by itself.

---

#### Blade Trap

You catch and redirect a weapon using the dagger's guard, spine or reinforced edge.

**Effects**
- After successfully defending against an adjacent melee weapon attack, attempt an opposed Dagger check.
- On success, the attacker suffers **-2 Accuracy** on its next weapon attack.
- You gain Advantage on your next attempt to disarm that weapon.
- Oversized or extremely heavy weapons may gain a bonus when resisting.

---

### Journeyman Techniques

> The Journeyman moves before intention becomes action.  
> A glance, tightened shoulder or shifting foot is enough to reveal where the next opening will appear.

#### Flurry of Steel

You unleash several rapid strikes against a nearby enemy.

**Effects**
- Spend an additional **Action Point** to make a second Dagger attack.
- The second attack suffers **-2 Accuracy**.
- Both attacks may target the same creature or different adjacent creatures.
- Each attack applies damage and conditions separately.

---

#### Disarming Cut

You slash across fingers, wrists and weapon straps.

**Effects**
- Make a Dagger attack against a weapon or the limb holding it.
- On success, the target must pass a Strength or Dexterity check or drop the held item.
- The attack deals reduced damage unless it scores a Critical Hit.
- Creatures with secured or integrated weapons may resist automatically.

---

#### Passing Blade

You strike while slipping beyond an opponent's position.

**Effects**
- Move through a space adjacent to a hostile creature and make one Dagger attack.
- On a successful hit, continue moving without provoking an ordinary Reaction from that creature.
- You must end in an unoccupied space.
- This technique cannot be used if your Movement has been reduced to zero.

---

#### Counterstab

You exploit the opening left by a missed attack.

**Effects**
- When an adjacent enemy misses you with a melee attack, use your Reaction to make one Dagger attack.
- Gain **+1 Accuracy** on the counterattack.
- The attack cannot trigger another counter effect.
- You must be able to see and reach the attacker.

---

### Adept Techniques

> The Adept sees anatomy and armour as a collection of narrow pathways.  
> Their blade needs only a finger's width to find something vital.

#### Deep Thrust

You commit to a precise thrust through an exposed opening.

**Effects**
- Spend one additional **Action Point** before making the attack.
- Ignore **3 Armour**.
- On a successful hit, roll one additional weapon damage die.
- This technique requires a dagger capable of making a piercing attack.

---

#### Nerve Strike

You target a sensitive nerve cluster or equivalent anatomical structure.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, a successful Dagger attack forces the target to make a Constitution Save.
- On failure, the target becomes **Dazed** until the end of its next turn.
- On a Critical Hit, the target may also lose its Reaction.
- Creatures without suitable anatomy may be immune.

---

#### Shadow Step

You use an enemy's body and attention to conceal your repositioning.

**Effects**
- After successfully striking a creature, move to another unoccupied space adjacent to it.
- The movement does not provoke an ordinary Reaction from that creature.
- Gain Advantage on your next Stealth check before the end of your turn.
- This technique does not make you invisible.

---

#### Opening Barrage

You exploit a target already pressured by another combatant.

**Effects**
- Gain **+2 Accuracy** against a creature adjacent to one of your allies.
- On the first successful hit each turn, deal **+2 Damage**.
- The allied creature must be active and capable of threatening the target.
- This technique does not apply when the ally is incapacitated.

---

### Master Techniques

> The Master no longer reacts to openings.  
> Through pressure, movement and deception, they decide where the opening must appear.

#### Dance of Knives

You move between nearby enemies while striking each in turn.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to move up to half your Movement.
- Make one Dagger attack against up to three different creatures passed during the movement.
- Roll separately against each target.
- These creatures cannot make ordinary Reactions against this movement.
- Each creature may be targeted only once.

---

#### Artery Sever

You deliver a precise cut intended to cause catastrophic blood loss.

**Effects**
- Spend one **Action Point** aiming before making the attack.
- On a Critical Hit, increase the target's Bleeding by two ranks, to the allowed maximum.
- If the target cannot Bleed, deal two additional weapon damage dice instead.
- Bosses and legendary creatures may reduce the resulting condition.

---

#### Vanishing Counter

You strike and immediately leave the enemy's reach.

**Effects**
- When an adjacent enemy misses you, use your Reaction to make one Dagger attack.
- After the attack, move up to **10 ft** without provoking an ordinary Reaction from that enemy.
- The movement must end in an unoccupied space.
- You cannot use this movement while Grappled or Restrained.

---

#### Death by Degrees

Every small wound creates a greater opening for the next.

**Effects**
- Consecutive successful Dagger attacks against the same target gain **+1 Damage**.
- The bonus stacks up to **+5 Damage**.
- The bonus resets when you miss, attack another creature or the combat ends.
- Each hit must deal at least one point of damage to increase the bonus.

---

### Grandmaster Techniques

> The Grandmaster's blade is seen only before the battle begins and after it ends.  
> Between those moments, there is only movement, silence and the sudden understanding of mortality.

#### Strike Between Heartbeats

You attack within an instant too brief for ordinary defence.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to make one Dagger attack with Advantage.
- Ignore all Armour granted by worn equipment.
- On a successful hit, roll two additional weapon damage dice.
- Natural Armour and magical barriers are not ignored.

---

#### Thousand Wounds Discipline

You unleash a sequence of rapid, precisely placed attacks.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, make up to four Dagger attacks.
- Each attack after the first suffers a cumulative **-1 Accuracy**.
- The attacks may target one creature or several creatures within reach.
- Each successful hit after the first deals reduced weapon damage.

---

#### Unseen Execution

You exploit complete surprise to deliver a devastating opening strike.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when attacking a creature that is unaware of you.
- Ignore all worn Armour on the attack.
- A Critical Hit rolls three additional weapon damage dice.
- Once the target becomes aware of you, this technique cannot be used against it again during that encounter.

---

#### Blade Beyond Sight

You have achieved legendary mastery of speed, placement and dagger control.

**Effects**
- The first Dagger attack you make each round has Advantage.
- Dagger attacks count as Magical for overcoming resistances.
- Once per encounter, turn a failed Dagger attack into a successful hit.
- Critical Hits with daggers inflict **Bleeding** in addition to their normal effects.

---

> *"A dagger does not challenge strength. It waits for strength to leave something unguarded."*

## Checks

Use **Dexterity** as the primary characteristic and **Agility** as the supporting characteristic when the GM calls for a Daggers check.

## Training

# Hammer Wielding

## Overview

Hammer Wielding Techniques represent specialized combat maneuvers learned through mastery of the **Hammer Wielding** skill. Rather than every skilled hammer user fighting the same way, techniques allow each warrior to develop their own unique combat style.

Whenever a character reaches a new **Hammer Wielding Skill Rank**, they may choose **one** technique from the four techniques available at that rank.

Once learned, a technique becomes a permanent part of the character's fighting style unless retrained through a rare method determined by the GM.

Hammer techniques are considered **Skill Techniques**, not Talents. Any character proficient with hammers may learn them regardless of class, allowing warriors, paladins, clerics, blacksmiths and other adventurers to specialize in their preferred style of combat.

---

**Primary Characteristic:** Strength  
**Secondary Characteristic:** Constitution

## Ranks

### Learning Techniques

| Skill Rank | Techniques Available | Techniques Learned |
|------------|----------------------|--------------------|
| Novice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Initiate | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Apprentice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Journeyman | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Adept | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Master | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Grandmaster | 4 | Choose 1 |

**Maximum Techniques Known:** **7**

---

### Novice Techniques

#### Crushing Blow
Your strikes carry overwhelming force capable of denting armour and breaking bones.

**Effects**
- Gain **+2 Damage** with Hammer attacks.
- Ignore **1 Natural Armour**.

---

#### Brace
You plant yourself before every swing, making yourself difficult to move.

**Effects**
- After making a Hammer attack, gain **+1 AC** until the start of your next turn.
- This bonus is lost if you moved more than half your movement before attacking.

---

#### Bone Rattler
A heavy impact leaves opponents struggling to regain their footing.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, creatures damaged by your Hammer lose **5 ft Movement** until the start of their next turn.

---

#### Mason's Strike
Your understanding of impact allows you to shatter objects with ease.

**Effects**
- Deal double damage against structures, barricades, doors and objects.
- Gain Advantage on Strength checks made to break objects using a Hammer.

---

### Initiate Techniques

#### Armour Breaker
Repeated blows gradually destroy an opponent's protection.

**Effects**
- Once per round, reduce a target's Armour by **1** until combat ends.
- Maximum reduction of **3 Armour**.

---

#### Driving Swing
Each strike forces your opponent backwards.

**Effects**
- Push a creature **5 ft** after a successful Hammer attack.
- Large or larger creatures instead lose **5 ft Movement** next turn.

---

#### Skullcracker
A perfectly placed strike leaves enemies dazed.

**Effects**
- Critical Hits inflict **Dazed** until the end of the target's next turn.

---

#### Momentum Strike
The weight of your hammer carries into another enemy.

**Effects**
- When you defeat a creature, immediately make a free Hammer attack against another adjacent enemy.

---

### Apprentice Techniques

#### Earthshaker
Your hammer sends tremors through the battlefield.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, strike the ground.
- Creatures within **5 ft** must succeed on an Agility Save or become **Off Balance**.

---

#### Crushing Momentum
Every strike grows heavier than the last.

**Effects**
- Consecutive attacks against the same target gain **+1 Damage**.
- Maximum **+5 Damage**.

---

#### Sunder
You know exactly where equipment is weakest.

**Effects**
- Critical Hits may damage:
  - Armour
  - Shields
  - Weapons

---

#### Giant Slayer
You specialize in bringing down enormous foes.

**Effects**
- Gain **+2 Damage** against Large or larger creatures.
- Ignore the first point of Damage Reduction they possess.

---

### Journeyman Techniques

#### Shockwave
The force of your strikes ripples outward.

**Effects**
- Once every three rounds, create a **10 ft cone**.
- Enemies take minor damage and are pushed backwards.

---

#### Unstoppable Swing
Your attack continues through fallen enemies.

**Effects**
- If your attack defeats an enemy, immediately attack another adjacent creature.
- The second attack deals **50% Damage**.

---

#### Pulverise
Your hammer excels at destroying brittle materials.

**Effects**
- Deal double damage against crystal, bone, ice and similar materials.

---

#### Iron Resolve
Nothing interrupts your attack.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage against effects that would interrupt or prevent your Hammer attacks.

---

### Adept Techniques

#### Quaking Slam
A devastating impact throws enemies from their feet.

**Effects**
- Slam the ground.
- Enemies within **10 ft** must succeed on an Agility Save or fall **Prone**.

---

#### Dragon Breaker
Your strikes are capable of cracking dragon scales.

**Effects**
- Ignore **3 Natural Armour**.
- Deal bonus damage against Dragons and Constructs.

---

#### Avalanche
Your offensive pressure becomes relentless.

**Effects**
- Consecutive Hammer attacks gain **+1 Accuracy**.
- Bonus resets when an attack misses.

---

#### Fortress Breaker
Even castles fear your hammer.

**Effects**
- Deal increased damage against fortifications, siege weapons and magical barriers.

---

### Master Techniques

#### Meteor Hammer
You descend like a falling star.

**Effects**
- Leap to a nearby location.
- Upon landing, enemies in the area take damage and are pushed away.

---

#### Cataclysm Strike
One devastating swing capable of ending battles.

**Effects**
- Requires **2 Action Points**.
- Deals massive bonus damage.
- Ignores half of the target's Armour.

---

#### Mountain Stance
You become an immovable object.

**Effects**
- Cannot be pushed or knocked Prone.
- Gain Resistance against forced movement.

---

#### Echoing Impact
The force of your strike continues beyond the initial blow.

**Effects**
- Adjacent enemies take minor Shockwave damage after a successful Hammer attack.

---

### Grandmaster Techniques

#### Worldbreaker
A legendary strike said to split mountains.

**Effects**
- Create a massive shockwave around the point of impact.
- Structures suffer catastrophic damage.
- Creatures in the area are knocked **Prone** and become **Staggered**.

---

#### Dragon's Doom
No creature is too mighty to withstand your hammer.

**Effects**
- Against Huge or larger creatures:
  - Ignore all Natural Armour.
  - Deal increased Critical Damage.
  - Critical Hits may Stun the target.

---

#### Earthsplitter
The battlefield itself yields beneath your hammer.

**Effects**
- Create a large fissure across the battlefield.
- The fissure becomes Difficult Terrain.
- Smaller creatures may fall into the opening.

---

#### Titan's Legacy
You have achieved perfect mastery of the hammer.

**Effects**
- The first Hammer attack each round has Advantage.
- Critical Hits deal one additional damage die.
- Hammer attacks count as Magical for overcoming resistances.

---

> *"A sword may win a duel. A hammer decides the fate of kingdoms."*

## Checks

Use **Strength** as the primary characteristic and **Constitution** as the supporting characteristic when the GM calls for a Hammer Wielding check.

---

#### Crushing Counter

**Effects**
- When an adjacent enemy misses a melee attack against you, make a single Mace attack as a Reaction.

---

#### Juggernaut

Nothing slows your advance.

**Effects**
- Ignore Difficult Terrain while moving toward an enemy.
- Gain Resistance against forced movement.

---

### Adept Techniques

#### Pulverising Blow

One strike can crush even the strongest armour.

**Effects**
- Ignore **3 Natural Armour**.
- Deal increased damage against Constructs and heavily armoured enemies.

---

#### Fracture

Your blows leave lasting injuries.

**Effects**
- Critical Hits inflict **Bleeding** or **Weakened** (your choice).

---

#### Warbreaker

Your mace excels against military formations.

**Effects**
- Deal bonus damage against enemies wielding Shields or wearing Heavy Armour.

---

#### Earthbound

Your stance is unwavering.

**Effects**

entries.body:
# Swordsmanship

## Overview

Swordsmanship Skill Techniques represent specialised attacks, guards, counters and movement patterns learned through mastery of the **Swordsmanship** skill.

A swordsman does more than swing a blade. They learn how to control distance, read an opponent's stance, redirect incoming attacks and place strikes where they are most effective. As their mastery grows, their sword becomes an extension of their body, allowing them to shift between offence and defence with little wasted movement.

Whenever a character reaches a new **Swordsmanship Skill Rank**, they may choose **one technique** from the four techniques available at that rank.

Once selected, a technique becomes part of the character's swordsmanship training unless it is replaced through retraining approved by the GM.

Swordsmanship Techniques are **Skill Techniques**, not Talents. Most techniques have no inherent resource cost. Particularly strenuous techniques may require additional Action Points or Stamina when they involve repeated attacks, extreme movement or sustained defensive pressure.

---

**Primary Characteristic:** Dexterity  
**Secondary Characteristic:** Strength

## Ranks

### Learning Techniques

| Skill Rank | Techniques Available | Techniques Learned |
|---|---:|---:|
| Novice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Initiate | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Apprentice | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Journeyman | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Adept | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Master | 4 | Choose 1 |
| Grandmaster | 4 | Choose 1 |

**Maximum Techniques Known:** **7**

---

### Novice Techniques

#### Controlled Slash

You strike with measured force rather than relying on wild swings.

**Effects**
- Gain **+1 Accuracy** with Sword attacks.
- Reduce penalties caused by minor distractions or unstable footing.
- This benefit does not apply while Prone or Restrained.

---

#### Guarded Stance

You keep your blade between yourself and your opponent.

**Effects**
- After making a Sword attack, gain **+1 AC** until the start of your next turn.
- The bonus ends if you are disarmed.
- You cannot benefit while using the sword for another two-handed action.

---

#### Quick Draw

You can draw your weapon and immediately enter combat.

**Effects**
- Draw a sword without interrupting ordinary movement.
- Gain Advantage on checks made to ready your sword under pressure.
- During the first round of combat, drawing your sword does not increase the Action Point cost of your first attack.

---

#### Measured Footwork

You maintain proper distance through careful movement.

**Effects**
- Gain Advantage when resisting attempts to force you out of melee reach.
- You may shift **5 ft** after a successful Sword attack without provoking an ordinary Reaction from that target.
- This movement cannot pass through occupied spaces.

---

### Initiate Techniques

#### Locking Guard

You trap an opponent's weapon against your blade.

**Effects**
- After successfully defending against an adjacent melee weapon attack, you may attempt to lock the attacking weapon.
- Make an opposed Swordsmanship check against the attacker.
- On success, gain Advantage on your next attack against that creature.
- The lock ends if either creature moves out of reach or releases its weapon.

---

#### Long Slash

You perform a broad, committed cut.

**Effects**
- Spend an additional **Action Point** before making a Sword attack.
- On a successful hit, deal **+2 Damage**.
- The attack may strike a second adjacent creature if it is positioned beside the original target.
- The second creature takes reduced damage.

---

#### Deflecting Blade

You use the flat and edge of your sword to redirect attacks.

**Effects**
- Use your Reaction when targeted by a visible melee weapon attack.
- Gain **+2 AC** against that attack.
- The bonus applies only to the triggering attack.
- You must be holding a sword and able to move your weapon.

---

#### Opening Cut

You target gaps created by an opponent's movement.

**Effects**
- Gain **+2 Damage** against a creature that moved into your melee reach during its previous turn.
- The bonus applies only to your first attack against that creature.
- Forced movement does not activate this technique.

---

### Apprentice Techniques

#### Riposte

You immediately answer a poorly placed attack.

**Effects**
- When an adjacent enemy misses you with a melee attack, use your Reaction to make one Sword attack against it.
- The attack cannot trigger another Riposte.
- You must be able to see the attacker.

---

#### Hampering Cut

You target muscles and joints to restrict movement.

**Effects**
- Once per turn, a creature damaged by your sword loses **10 ft Movement** until the end of its next turn.
- On a Critical Hit, the target also cannot take the Sprint action during that time.
- Creatures without vulnerable limbs may be immune.

---

#### Half-Sword Grip

You grip the blade to guide the point into armour gaps.

**Effects**
- When wielding an appropriate sword, you may enter a Half-Sword Grip.
- While using this grip, ignore **2 Armour**.
- Your weapon damage die is reduced by one step while using the technique.
- Changing grip may be done once during your turn.

---

#### Sweeping Guard

You use broad blade movements to control nearby space.

**Effects**
- Enemies moving through your melee reach provoke a Sword attack as a Reaction.
- On a successful hit, their movement immediately ends.
- You may use this technique once per round.
- Creatures using teleportation or forced movement do not trigger it.

---

### Journeyman Techniques

#### Flowing Assault

Each successful strike carries into the next movement.

**Effects**
- After hitting with a Sword attack, gain **+1 Accuracy** on your next Sword attack during the same turn.
- The bonus stacks up to **+2 Accuracy**.
- All accumulated bonuses are lost when you miss or your turn ends.

---

#### Pommel Strike

You reverse your weapon and strike with the pommel.

**Effects**
- Make a close-range blunt attack using your sword.
- On a successful hit, deal reduced weapon damage.
- The target must succeed on a Constitution Save or become **Dazed** until the end of its next turn.
- This technique may be used once per encounter against the same creature.

---

#### Blade Bind

You engage an opponent's weapon and control its position.

**Effects**
- After hitting a creature wielding a melee weapon, choose to deal reduced damage and initiate a Blade Bind.
- The target suffers **-2 Accuracy** on weapon attacks against creatures other than you.
- The bind lasts until the start of your next turn or until either creature leaves reach.
- Two-handed and oversized weapons may gain a bonus when resisting the bind.

---

#### Passing Strike

You cut an enemy while moving beyond them.

**Effects**
- Move through a space adjacent to a hostile creature and make one Sword attack.
- On a successful hit, continue moving without provoking an ordinary Reaction from that creature.
- You must end your movement in an unoccupied space.
- This technique cannot be used while your movement is reduced to zero.

---

### Adept Techniques

#### Armour-Seeking Thrust

You deliver a precise thrust through a vulnerable opening.

**Effects**
- Spend one additional **Action Point** before making the attack.
- Ignore **4 Armour**.
- On a Critical Hit, roll one additional weapon damage die.
- This technique requires a sword capable of thrusting.

---

#### Blade Arc

Your sword travels through several enemies in one continuous motion.

**Effects**
- Make one Sword attack against up to three adjacent creatures within your reach.
- Roll separately against each target.
- Attacks after the first deal reduced weapon damage.
- This technique may be used once every three rounds.

---

#### Perfect Parry

You turn aside an attack with minimal movement.

**Effects**
- Use your Reaction when hit by a visible melee weapon attack.
- Make a Swordsmanship check against the attacker's result.
- On success, reduce the attack's damage to zero.
- On failure, reduce the damage by an amount determined by your Swordsmanship modifier.
- This technique may be used once per round.

---

#### Duelist's Focus

You concentrate entirely on a single opponent.

**Effects**
- Choose one visible creature within melee reach.
- Gain **+2 Accuracy** and **+1 AC** against that creature.
- You suffer **-1 AC** against attacks made by other creatures.
- The focus ends when you change targets, lose sight of the creature or move away from it.

---

### Master Techniques

#### Whirlwind of Steel

You become the centre of a storm of blades.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to attack every hostile creature within your Sword reach.
- Roll one attack against each creature.
- Each attack deals normal weapon damage.
- You cannot use this technique while Restrained or in an area too narrow to swing your sword.

---

#### Severing Strike

You deliver a powerful cut intended to cripple or remove a vulnerable limb.

**Effects**
- Spend one Action Point aiming before making the attack.
- On a Critical Hit, inflict a severe limb injury appropriate to the target.
- Against creatures immune to limb injuries, deal two additional weapon damage dice instead.
- Bosses and legendary creatures may resist permanent injuries.

---

#### Mirror Guard

Your blade reacts to attacks from every direction.

**Effects**
- Until the start of your next turn, gain **+2 AC** against melee weapon attacks.
- You may use Perfect Parry without consuming your Reaction once during this duration.
- Activating Mirror Guard requires one Action Point.
- The technique ends if you are disarmed or incapacitated.

---

#### Relentless Blade

Defeating one opponent allows you to immediately pressure another.

**Effects**
- When you reduce a creature to zero Health with a Sword attack, move up to half your Movement.
- You may then make one Sword attack against another creature within reach.
- This additional attack may occur only once per round.
- The movement must bring you closer to a hostile creature.

---

### Grandmaster Techniques

#### Sword Saint's Cut

Your blade passes through defence before the enemy recognises the strike.

**Effects**
- Spend **2 Action Points** to make one Sword attack with Advantage.
- Ignore all Armour granted by worn equipment and shields.
- On a successful hit, roll two additional weapon damage dice.
- Natural Armour and magical barriers are not ignored.

---

#### Thousand-Cut Discipline

Your sword moves too quickly for ordinary eyes to follow.

**Effects**
- Once per encounter, make up to four Sword attacks.
- Each attack after the first suffers a cumulative **-1 Accuracy**.
- The attacks may target one creature or several creatures within reach.
- Each attack requires its normal Action Point cost, reduced by one for the duration to a minimum of one.

---

#### Unbroken Counter

Every attack made against you creates an opportunity.

**Effects**
- Once per round, when you successfully avoid or parry a melee attack, immediately make one Sword attack against the attacker.
- This counter does not consume your Reaction.
- The attack cannot trigger another counter effect.
- You must be holding a sword and capable of acting.

---

#### Blade Without Equal

You have achieved legendary mastery of swordsmanship.

**Effects**
- The first Sword attack you make each round has Advantage.
- Sword attacks count as Magical for overcoming resistances.
- Once per encounter, turn a failed Sword attack into a successful hit.
- Critical Hits with swords deal one additional weapon damage die.

---

> *"The sword is not mastered when the hand becomes fast. It is mastered when every movement has purpose."*

## Checks

Use **Dexterity** as the primary characteristic and **Strength** as the supporting characteristic when the GM calls for a Swordsmanship check.
